title: Gradischar 2022 costal cartilage secant tensile modulus

quantity.name: secant tensile modulus
quantity.definition: secant modulus between 20 N and 40 N in axial tension (1.3e-3 /s)

source.authors: Gradischar A, Lebschy C, Krach W, Krall M, Fediuk M, Gieringer A, Smolle-Juttner F, Hammer N, Beyer B, Smolle J, Schafer U
source.sample: 12 costal cartilage samples (ribs 2-6, left/right) from 2 fresh unembalmed male cadavers

protocol.summary: Costal cartilage with rib part (perichondrium status: see paper, Fig 1 cross-section shown without perichondrium), moulded fixation; rib end clamped and cartilage loaded as cantilever (force at sternal end, max 4 N) in anterior (B1), superior (B2), posterior (B3), inferior (B4) directions -> bending moduli from elliptical cross-section beam theory; torsion via force couple (max 5 N, 175 Nmm) in two directions (GT1, GT2); tension along the cartilage axis to 50 N at 1.3e-3 /s -> secant modulus between 20 and 40 N. Each test 3 times, 2nd and 3rd used. Samples refrigerated at 5-7 C.
how_to_simulate: Model the costal cartilage as a cantilever fixed at the rib with elliptical cross-section a x b and free length l (Table 2)
Apply the small tip force (<=4 N bending, <=175 Nmm torsion, <=50 N tension) in the stated direction
Back-calculate modulus with beam theory as the authors did, or compare tip deflection/twist

extraction.check_notes: Table 2 from text layer (digital PDF), checked row by row. Median row as printed. * bending moduli computed with median shear modulus; ** median shear modulus substituted (no torsion test) - flagged in row notes.

pass_rule.rule: |model - mean| <= 1 SD (or inside [min, max] when no SD)
